comments.body:
Split pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1496

**The seams this ticket originally proposed are both unsafe.** Worth recording, because the reason is invisible from the file itself.

Two unit tests load this conftest by path and drive it with `monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_request", fake)`. That rebinds a name in *conftest's* globals, so it only reaches callers whose own module globals are that namespace. Move `_request` — or any of its patched-through callers (`_create_scratch_project`, `_assert_project_capabilities`, `_leaked_harness_tokens`, `_sweep_leaked_harness_tokens`, `wait_for_jira_dc_ready`, `jira_dc_project`) — to a sibling module and the moved function resolves the REAL `_request`. The unit tier then starts issuing live HTTP. That fails OPEN: nothing errors, the stub just silently stops applying. Both clusters the ticket named (PAT sweep, scratch-project provisioning) are entirely inside that set.

**What was extracted instead:** the J11 store-copy / DC-client cluster — `dc_transport`, `dc_store_copy_repo`, `bound_dc_issue`. It already carried its own banner comment in the file explaining it sits in conftest only because two sibling suites need it; `bound_dc_issue` consumes the other two and all three draw on `_dc_support`, so it is a real call-graph cluster, not a slice. No unit test references any member. 203 lines moved to `_dc_fixtures.py` (248 with its header, clear of the 100-line floor); conftest is 758.

Mechanics: conftest re-imports the three names so pytest still collects them as its own attributes (verified with `pytest --fixtures`), the sibling directory goes on `sys.path` the same way `_TESTS_DIR`/`engine_dir()`/`_SCRIPTS_DIR` already do, and the base URL reaches the moved fixtures via a new session-scoped `jira_dc_base_url` fixture rather than a second copy of `_BASE`.

**Coverage added** (3 cells in `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py`): the fixture surface survives the by-path load; every monkeypatched name is still *defined* in conftest, not merely re-exported into it; and the file stays within the cap read from `.github/module-size-limit.txt` rather than a restated number. The middle cell is the one that earns its keep — it is the only thing standing between a future split and a silent un-stubbing that would surface 35 minutes into a live harness run.

**One pre-existing guard needed widening.** `tests/unit/test_live_dc_isolation_controls_59b2.py` greps the fixture source for `for cloud_var in CLOUD_CREDENTIAL_VARS:` to prove the credential list is not duplicated — and read `conftest.py` by name. Since `dc_store_copy_repo` holds that loop, the guard would have reported it DELETED when it had only moved. It now scans the harness's whole fixture surface, asserting the same invariant without being keyed to a filename. It caught the move correctly, which is a point in its favour.

compiled_state.description:
Observed during bug 941b-f049-5f29-4410's rebar-debug pass.

AGENTS.md sets a target of 200-500 LOC per file and a **hard cap of 800**. The CI module-size
gate that enforces it covers `src/rebar` only, so this file is over the cap without failing
the build.

    932 tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py

It was 917 before 941b and is 932 after (941b removed the session-start field gate and the
`_CAPABILITY_FIELD_CONFIRM_BUDGET_S` cap, and added the provisioning evidence that explains
why). So 941b did not create the condition and did not meaningfully worsen it, but it also did
not fix it, and splitting it was out of that bug's scope.

## The binding constraint: the monkeypatch surface must not move

Two unit tests load this conftest **by path**
(`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`) and drive it as `harness.<name>`. Critically they
do not merely *read* attributes, they **rebind** them:

    tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py:101  monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_request", _fake)
    tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py:104  monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_random_project_key", ...)
    tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py:92       monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_request", _fake)

A patch on the conftest module object only reaches callers whose **own module globals** are
that same namespace. So moving a *stubbed callee* (`_request`) or any of its *callers*
(`_create_scratch_project`, `_assert_project_capabilities`, `_leaked_harness_tokens`,
`_sweep_leaked_harness_tokens`, `wait_for_jira_dc_ready`, `jira_dc_project`) out of conftest
silently un-stubs the network: the moved function resolves `_request` in the NEW module's
globals, which the test never patched. That fails open — the unit tests would attempt real
HTTP instead of erroring clearly.

The two seams the original filing suggested (the PAT sweep cluster and the scratch-project
provisioning cluster) are therefore both **unsafe**: every member of both is either a
patch target or a patched-through caller.

## The seam that is safe

The **J11 store-copy / DC-client fixture cluster** — `dc_transport`, `dc_store_copy_repo`,
`bound_dc_issue` — already carries its own banner comment in the file explaining it lives in
conftest solely because two sibling suites need it. It is a genuine existing call-graph
cluster (`bound_dc_issue` consumes `dc_store_copy_repo` and `dc_transport`; all three draw on
`_dc_support`), and no member of it is referenced by either unit test, patched or otherwise.
Roughly 205 LOC, so the extracted module clears the 100-LOC floor and conftest lands near 730.

## Plan

- Extract `dc_transport`, `dc_store_copy_repo`, and `bound_dc_issue`, with their explanatory
  banner comment, into a sibling `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py`.
- **Re-export them into conftest's namespace** with a top-level
  `from _dc_fixtures import bound_dc_issue, dc_store_copy_repo, dc_transport`, so pytest
  still collects them from conftest exactly as today (pytest registers fixtures found as
  attributes of the conftest module, regardless of where they were defined).
- Resolve the package-less sibling import the same way the file already resolves
  `_engine_path` and `jira_dc_field_readiness`: insert the conftest's own directory on
  `sys.path` before the import, rather than relying on pytest's prepend-mode insertion.
- Thread the base URL through the **fixture graph** rather than duplicating the `_BASE`
  constant into the new module: add a session-scoped `jira_dc_base_url` fixture in conftest
  and have the extracted fixtures depend on it. This avoids a second copy of the env-var
  default drifting from the first.
- Leave `_request`, `_field_request`, `wait_for_jira_dc_ready`, `_random_project_key`,
  `track_issue`, `dc_request`, the PAT cluster, and the provisioning cluster **in conftest**,
  untouched, so the monkeypatch surface above is bit-for-bit preserved.
- Add a regression test asserting the loaded-by-path conftest still exposes the fixture
  surface, so a future move that breaks re-export fails at the unit tier instead of 35
  minutes into a live harness run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` is at or under 800 LOC
- [ ] the split follows an existing call-graph seam and creates no file under 100 LOC
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py` and `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py`
      still pass (both load the conftest by PATH, so a move must keep the loaded module's
      surface intact)
- [ ] every symbol the unit tests monkeypatch, and every caller that must observe those
      patches, remains defined in conftest
- [ ] the moved fixtures are re-exported into conftest's namespace and remain resolvable by
      `pytest --fixtures tests/external/live_jira_dc/`
- [ ] lint and typecheck pass
